reason: Decisive defect is c1 (confirmed, in_scope): the k-loop (kernel.py:41-54) applies no K-dimension bounds mask to any of the g_idx, b_packed, or A loads, and num_pid_k = cdiv(K, BLOCK_SIZE_K=16) rounds up. Runtime evidence c1.e1 (tool event t9) is a controlled probe pair: K=128 (multiple of 16) reproduced C = A @ dequant(B) exactly (max_abs_err 0.0 vs ref_absmax 51.0), while K=72 — a legal 4-bit packing (9 int32 rows) with group_size=64 and a trailing partial group — raised a CUDA illegal memory access (cudaErrorIllegalAddress). Zero codes were restricted to 0..14 in that probe so the c3 zero-point question cannot confound it. Scope: this artifact provides no test.py or get_inputs (test_code is empty), so problem.txt is the operative contract, and it explicitly requires correct dequantized matmul "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size, where the trailing partial group is still a group of its own." K=72 is exactly such a K and is admitted by the host wrapper signature (kernel.py:61-69). The reference is well-defined and finite for this input, so this is a genuine correctness/robustness failure, not a reference-undefined case. Non-decisive notes: c2 (unmasked N loads) was rebutted as stated — N=48 matched the reference exactly with no fault, the over-read landing in allocator slack — so it is only a latent UB/portability observation and was never established as in_scope. c3 is confirmed as a real behavioral divergence (kernel implements zeros+1 with no `& maxq`, matching the unwrapped variant exactly and differing from the wrapped AutoGPTQ convention by >100% relative error when a zero nibble is 15) but its scope stays unknown: problem.txt states plain `zero` with no +1 or wrap convention, so no artifact pins which of {zero, zero+1, (zero+1)&maxq} is required. I set c3 aside as unresolved and do not rest the verdict on it; c1 alone is sufficient.
